decisions.what: T-103b FAILED the gate on one clause ('confirmed by test/astro.test.js') and was reverted rather than conductor-patched, even though the repair is a single word and this is the run's last open must-have

The cost is real and named: one more k=1 cycle spent on a one-clause repair, with the run's last must-have still open. decisions.what: the gate's decisive check was a HEDGE-PARITY comparison against the module and test, not a reading of the prose

That makes the finding reproducible by anyone, and it produced the falsifiability discriminator that justifies the fail: if the implementation were wrong at an unsampled instant inside the domain, the module comment stays true and the README sentence becomes false. Generalisable beyond this item - a docs claim may be checked against the hedge vocabulary of the code it documents.

decisions.what: the 'module comment gloss wider than the code' pattern reached its FOURTH instance (T-110, T-112, T-113, now T-105) and is promoted from one-off backlog rows to a candidate playbook lesson for WRAP_UP distillation

decisions.what: T-110's fix accepted in the 'half-open range of years 1000-3000' framing rather than 'years 1000-2999', and the residual README readability question deliberately NOT filed as a fifth prose item

decisions.what: the gate’s central check was an INSTRUMENTED SWEEP of the real branch, not a reading of the source — and it is what upgraded the item from ‘true by inspection’ to ‘true by measurement’
decisions.why: Reading `else if (cover < 0.88) HALF; else ROUND_LIMB` proves the fix is consistent with the source, but it does NOT prove the disc ever actually reaches that branch below full lit — if cover only ever hit 1.0 in practice, the old prose would have been complete after all and this item would have been churn. So renderLine was driven over a 20,000-step synodic sweep in both hemispheres against an instrumented COPY of render.js (repo source untouched): 2,924 of 33,192 round-limb draws land at cover<1.0, least-lit 0.887324. The sweep also checked the converse, which a one-directional check would have missed: outer cells with cover>=0.88 number EXACTLY 33,192, the same as the round-limb draws, so ‘0.88’ is the precise condition and not merely a sufficient one. Generalizable: a comment describing a branch is verifiable by instrumenting the branch and counting which side of it real inputs land on.

decisions.what: three gate flags (C4a, C4b, C4c) were traced to my own instrument and the instrument was repaired; each widening was paired with a strictly stronger assertion, and the normalizer was then falsified against HEAD
decisions.why: C4a swept `git ls-files`, so it flagged .swarm/backlog.json, .swarm/journal.md and the cycle-12 evidence file — the RECORD of the defect, which must keep the phrase ‘declines to establish’ to stay legible; product scope is src/, test/, README.md, REPORT.md, where the hit count is zero. C4b/C4c matched literal strings containing spaces while the edit had reflowed both passages, so ‘East Asian\nWidth class’ and ‘has not\n * been established’ spanned line breaks. decisions.what: T-132's acceptance is WIDENED at the retry rather than a second item being filed for the newly-found apostrophe truncation (moon "it's" -> 'unexpected argument 'it''), and the widening is forced by evidence

It is: the empty-token defect and the apostrophe-truncation defect are the SAME line of code and the SAME mechanism -- node:util quoting a token that itself contains quote characters. The measurement proves any rule that names the empty token must also handle a leading apostrophe, because both arise from the spurious pair; the narrow instance fix is provably regressive, and attempt 1 IS that narrow fix. Filing a separate item would guarantee a second builder rediscovering the same regression on the same line. Also worth naming plainly: the apostrophe truncation is live on main right now, is more reachable than the empty case, and was found by the gate, not by the scan that filed the item.

decisions.what: T-132 retries at OPUS, one ladder rung up from sonnet, despite gear 1 setting demote=true and premium sitting at opus_used_pct 96 under trickle posture

Applying demotion after escalation returns the item to the tier that just produced a plausible, green, wrong fix. The evidence here is specifically that sonnet asserted an unverified empirical claim about a third-party library as though verified -- the failure mode a rung up is most likely to change. One item at one rung is also the cheapest possible expression of that.

decisions.what: T-132 retried at SONNET, not the opus the cycle-34 ladder escalation named

Spending premium at 96% used to re-derive a table that already exists on disk would be paying for the same insight twice. The gate, not the model tier, is what caught attempt 1 and it is unchanged in strength.

decisions.what: the gate derives the true token by stripping node:util's fixed sentence templates, and additionally compares it against the argv element the conductor itself passed - never by scanning for quotes
decisions.why: Quote-scanning IS the mechanism under test. A gate that recovered the token the same way the fix does would agree with any rule the builder shipped, including attempt 1's wrong one, which was green on 124 tests. Template stripping is a genuinely different derivation, and it fails loudly if node:util ever reworders - so the gate doubles as the wording tripwire. The argv comparison is the stronger discriminator still: for positional cases the conductor knows the exact string it passed, and no degenerate implementation can reproduce an arbitrary input string it never saw. This is the transferable form of the cycle-34 lesson (execute the third party, do not reason about it), tightened by one turn.

The cycle-8/T-111 and cycle-17 disposition (do not fail an item whose acceptance passed IN FULL over a nuance) does not apply, because this clause did not pass at all. The item's entire value is future-conditional, so a defect in how it behaves under the exact future event it governs -- a regeneration of the table -- is central, not peripheral. Not conductor-patched, per the standing cycle-7 rule; that rule bites hardest here because the conductor authored both the item text and the diagnosis.

decisions.what: the reachability guard cannot be made complete by widening its sweep; attempt 2 must change the guard's SHAPE (escalate-on-failure, or a documented bound) rather than its window constants
decisions.why: measured, not argued: the distinct (name, percent) set is 209 at 120 days, 212 at 250 days, still 212 at 1-min/10-year resolution (5,256,001 samples), and 213 at 5-min/30-year -- the 213th (waning crescent|46%) is invisible to the 10-year fine sweep. The three cycle-39 retype mutants stay unreachable even at 1-min/10-year, so the guard's discriminating power survives a much wider search -- which is what makes an escalate-only-on-failure shape viable where a bigger constant is not.

decisions.what: T-141's end-to-end QA was run CONDUCTOR-INLINE with zero agent tiers spent, and the harness derived its hemisphere expectation from README's own north|south table rather than from the renderer

Gear 1 under a 0%-premium trickle posture makes any agent-dispatched QA the expensive option, and cycle.md step 5's FALLBACK explicitly permits conductor-inline QA when the workflow is unavailable (Workflow is review-gated in a headless -p session). For a stdout CLI the conductor can execute the real binary itself, which is strictly stronger evidence than a subagent's report of having done so - hard rule 2 says agent returns are claims, and this removes the claim step entirely. The harder problem was self-agreement: a QA harness that computes its expectation from the same renderer it is testing proves only that the code equals itself. Parsing README's 15-row north|south table into a mirror map, asserting the map is an involution, and requiring mirror(--north disc) == --south disc sources the contract from documentation and the behaviour from the binary, so the two can genuinely disagree. decisions.what: Three defects in my OWN mutation instrument were found and repaired mid-verification - fifth instance this run of my instrument being narrower than what it measures - and one of them had misreported a generator bug as a gap in the harness under test
decisions.why: The dangerous one was M9. It came back SURVIVED, which reads as 'the QA harness fails to check the disc width'. It was not: the generator had declared the mutation applied because a cosmetic edit changed the file's text, while the 5-cell constant it meant to change was never found (my regex \bCELLS never matches inside LINE_CELLS - underscore is a word character). Left alone I would have filed a false gap against a harness that was working. The repair is structural rather than per-mutant, per the cycles 8/9/19/29 precedent that every widening is paid for with a stronger assertion: exact unique source anchors replace regexes, and a NO-OP GUARD now compares the mutated binary's observable output against the unmutated one and reports NO-OP MUTANT rather than SURVIVED. The guard then failed twice itself, both in the safe direction (refusing to credit kills it could not see) - first because its probes pinned TZ=UTC, where M10's 'always north' is genuinely invisible, then because no probe combined --json with --help. The extracted rule is written into the file: a guard must be at least as observant as the harness it polices.

decisions.what: The QA found zero divergences, so the one finding filed (T-142) came from MEASURING which end-to-end surfaces the shipping suite pins - replaying the same ten mutants against `node --test` instead of against the harness

decisions.what: HI1 recorded as BOUNDARY on the stock-runtime domain, HOLE on the contract domain, after the conductor's FIRST gate returned a no-difference result that was worthless for it

The gate recording its own first answer as wrong — the second cycle running in which that has happened — is the mechanism working, not a defect in it.

decisions.what: HF3 recorded as a PROVEN boundary rather than a sampled one, with an explicit table contingency attached

Both passes reached this proof independently.

decisions.what: AA1 upgraded from "an unprotected behavior" to "a test that cannot fail", and filed as T-149 — a finding the conductor gate MISSED and the builder found
decisions.why: The gate witnessed AA1's divergence and stopped at 'untested guard'. The builder went further and identified why it survives: test/args.test.js:22 already asserts parseArgs(undefined) deep-equals the all-defaults object, and that test still passes under the mutation because node:util falls back to process.argv.slice(2), which under `node --test <file>` is empty — coincidentally matching the literal [] the truth code produces. Recorded as a miss on the gate's part, not absorbed silently — the point of two passes is that either one can catch the other.

decisions.what: IT3's BOUNDARY verdict UPHELD but its stated reason overturned: the builder's ground was that the shipped CLI has no --date flag, which is not the test that matters
decisions.why: package.json declares "main": "src/astro.js" and ships "files": ["bin/","src/","README.md"], and .swarm/CONTRACTS.md:17 documents computeMoon(date) as a public contract — a module consumer can pass any Date, so the module's reachable domain is strictly larger than the CLI's. An undocumented answer at an undocumented point is a boundary, not a hole. Practical consequence for T-146: IT3 does not enter the HOLE ranking, which stands unchanged at L1 > HI1 > O3 > L3.

decisions.what: T-148 FAILED on figure 4, but the four corrections the conductor INDEPENDENTLY re-measured were KEPT in the tree rather than reverted with the rest of the diff — a departure from the cycle-7/cycle-10 full-revert precedent, made deliberately.

decisions.what: the gate's decisive check was a DELTA-T ROBUSTNESS BAND, not a re-derivation at the builder's chosen DeltaT: the committed pair 0.6801/0.6475 holds for every dT in [48, 80] s, which makes the figure independent of the judgement call the item forced.
decisions.why: Cycle 58 settled this figure using dT = 58.3 s (published historical) and the retry builder independently chose 58.548 s from a different, better-scoped polynomial. Had my gate simply re-derived at the builder's DeltaT it would have confirmed the builder's ARITHMETIC, not the FIGURE -- and the item's whole failure mode at attempt 1 was a frame choice, not arithmetic. Sweeping dT from 40 to 80 s in 0.1 s steps converts 'the number is 0.6801 given dT = 58.3' into 'the number is 0.6801 unless DeltaT for 1992 was below ~48 s', which is a claim about the module rather than about anyone's constant. The two defensible candidates sit 10.3 s and 12.8 s inside the band's lower edge. Generalizable: when a published figure depends on a chosen parameter, the gate should measure the parameter's tolerance rather than re-run the choice.

known_issues.desc: terminal font/width variance for the Unicode glyphs is an untested surface (taste judge, product-not-demo axis). No automated check can cover it; requires a human look.

Disc glyphs span two East Asian Width classes (U+2591 and U+2590 are Neutral; U+2592/3/2588/258C/258F/2595 are Ambiguous). In terminals that render ambiguous-width as double (CJK locales, iTerm2 ambiguous-as-double, xterm -cjk_width) the disc is 5-9 columns instead of 5: the single line jitters between nights, the two-line form stops aligning, and the --block frame does not close. Verified by measurement. Not a typo but an upstream Unicode fact - no Block Elements subset gives a 4-step ramp plus a symmetric half-block pair in one width class. Correct in default Western-locale terminals. Documented in README; fix needs a glyph-set redesign, deliberately deferred rather than rushed at the buzzer. MACHINE-PINNED at cycle 5 (T-104): test/render.test.js derives the disc's glyph alphabet from actual renderLine/renderBlock output and asserts it against the documented partition, so the defect can no longer drift silently - the fix (glyph-set redesign) remains deliberately deferred. The pin also EXPOSED a scope gap in the README's glyph list: the disc additionally draws U+25D6/U+25D7 (round limb), which the width caveat never mentions. Tracked as T-109. DOC SIDE CLOSED cycle 9 (T-109): the README's width caveat now scopes its Block Element claim precisely and accounts for the two round-limb glyphs it had omitted, without asserting an EAW class the repo cannot check. The underlying width defect is UNFIXED and still deferred - only the documentation gap closed. MACHINE-CHECKED AT CYCLE 24 (T-121), which settled the two things this entry had only ever ASSERTED. (1) The hand-typed Neutral/Ambiguous partition above is CORRECT: all 8 documented Block Element glyphs match unicodedata UCD 15.0.0 exactly, 0 disagreements in either direction, and the drawn alphabet parsed out of src/render.js equals the set test/render.test.js documents. (2) The impossibility claim ('no Block Elements subset gives a 4-step ramp plus a symmetric half-block pair in one width class') was ENUMERATED rather than reasoned, and HOLDS -- under both KI-5's literal wording and a wider predicate covering all three handed pairs the renderer actually draws, and under a search pool widened from Block Elements alone to Block Elements + Geometric Shapes + Symbols for Legacy Computing. The mechanism is now named exactly: U+258C LEFT HALF BLOCK is Ambiguous while U+2590 RIGHT HALF BLOCK is Neutral, and that is the ONLY LEFT/RIGHT HALF BLOCK pair in any of the three ranges -- so the split is not one option among several, it is the sole candidate. The Neutral class independently fails for a second reason: it contains no full-fill glyph at all (nearest miss U+1FB86 UPPER SEVEN EIGHTHS BLOCK, density 0.875), because Unicode never assigned these families a distinct fully-filled codepoint -- that would duplicate U+2588, which is Ambiguous. Verified non-vacuous: the SHIPPED glyph set does satisfy the predicate once the single-class constraint is dropped, so this is a real constraint result and not an impossible requirement. Nearest misses a human relaxing 'half-block' should look at first: U+25D0/U+25D1 (CIRCLE WITH LEFT/RIGHT HALF BLACK, both Ambiguous) and U+25E7/U+25E8 (SQUARE WITH LEFT/RIGHT HALF BLACK, both Neutral) are same-class L/R pairs, but are circle/square motifs rather than fractional blocks, and the Neutral ramp ceiling still blocks the square pair. LIMITS, stated rather than buried: UCD class is a Unicode property, NOT a promise about any particular terminal; the sweep covers three justified ranges on UCD 15.0.0, not all of Unicode; Unicode 16's Octant symbols postdate this data and were NOT checked. SEVERITY UNCHANGED at medium and the issue stays OPEN: nothing was fixed. What changed is that the deferral is now evidence-backed instead of assertion-backed.

The bound is SAMPLED-clean, not proven, and is DECLARATIVE ONLY - nothing enforces it at runtime, deliberately, since a runtime guard is a behavior change the run's non-goals forbid. The issue stays OPEN at severity low because nothing was fixed: the two series still diverge at absurd epochs and the domain is declarative only. Bounded and documented is not the same as resolved. PROSE CORRECTED cycle 17 (T-110): all three sites that describe the domain (the src/astro.js doc comment, README's Accuracy paragraph, REPORT's KI-7 row) had glossed the half-open interval [Date.UTC(1000,0,1), Date.UTC(3000,0,1)) as an inclusive 'years 1000 through 3000' - one calendar year more than the constant defines and more than the test reaches (its last sample is 2999-07-02). package.json declares "license": "MIT" and "private": false, but the repo contains no LICENSE file (verified: no LICENSE* at the repo root). NOT fixed here on purpose: the MIT text needs a copyright holder line naming a legal person, which is the repo owner's decision and not one a build agent or the conductor may invent. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: the owner supplies the copyright line ('Copyright (c) <year> <holder>'); adding the standard MIT body around it is then a one-file mechanical change.
